lesson.title: BRICS and the Global South
lesson.summary: How emerging economies are challenging the Western order and reshaping global power.

blocks.text: BRICS is an acronym for Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa — a group of major emerging economies seeking greater representation in the global order.
In 2024, the bloc expanded to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates, nearly doubling its geographic representation and signaling a growing rejection of Western hegemony.

items: An alternative to the IMF and World Bank
Use of local currencies to bypass the dollar
Collective voice of the Global South in international negotiations

blocks.text: BRICS is not anti-West, but pro-Global South. — Cyril Ramaphosa
The bloc represents about 40% of the world's population and over 30% of global GDP, but still faces internal divisions — especially between China and India.

cards.back: Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa. In 2024 it expanded to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the UAE.

cards.front: Why does BRICS want to reduce dollar usage?
cards.back: To decrease dependence on a single currency and reduce vulnerability to Western economic sanctions.

cards.front: What is BRICS's main internal tension?
cards.back: The rivalry between China and India, which compete for regional influence and have unresolved territorial disputes.

quiz.question: What is one of BRICS's main goals?
options: Create a military alliance to rival NATO
Reduce the influence of the dollar and the IMF
Unify the currencies of member countries
Replace the UN as a global forum
quiz.explanation: BRICS seeks to create alternatives to the Western-led financial system, including using local currencies and building its own institutions.

quiz.question: Why is the 2024 BRICS expansion geopolitically significant?
options: Because it included European countries for the first time
Because it increased the bloc's combined military presence
Because it expanded Global South representation and signaled a challenge to Western hegemony
Because it created a common currency for international trade
quiz.explanation: The inclusion of Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the UAE expanded the bloc's geographic and political reach, reinforcing its position as an alternative to the West.
